text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT PAGER: Hosted runtime kvcache memory climb detected on us-west-2 GPUs. Severity: P2. Metric: kvcache_used_bytes per-gpu > 90% for 5m. Alert at 2798123456. Paging oncall: @Mila Chen.

Mila Chen: I’m on it. seeing steady climb on hostpool-gpu-7/8. spikes correlate with a few long prompt sessions.

Alex Park: putting quick snapshot here — heap / kvcache stats from hostpool-gpu-7: ```
KVCACHE_STATS {\n  total_slots: 32768\n  used_slots: 30112\n  estimated_bytes: 12898237440\n  largest_session: session-93fa (window=1,048,576 tokens)\n  top_sessions_by_bytes: [session-93fa, session-2a1b, session-f7c8]\n}```

Mila Chen: that largest_session is a single user with repeated long context concatenation. looks like continuous-batching + prefix caching keep growing kv entries.

Devon Shah: can we throttle prefetch for hosted runtime on that hostpool? A quick mitigation is to cap per-session prefetch and shrink batch window.

Laura Kim: create hotpatch: reduce continuous_batch_window from 128 -> 32, prefetch_max_entries_per_session  -> 50, and aggressive eviction threshold to 80%. prepping patch now.

Chris Ortega: marking impacted routes: /v1/chat/stream (model: rdx-large-open) — traffic ~12k rps across pool, about 5% hitting long-prompt clients. Customer-visible symptoms: tail latency spikes and 429s as GPU memory hits host-level OOM protection.

Samira Patel: FYI support already has one enterprise customer (acme-marketing) reporting timeouts. Not yet widespread billing impact but SLA risk.

Mila Chen: rolling a quick config hotfix to hostpool-gpu-7/8 as a canary, will watch for memory regression. Command I'm running: ```
redwoodctl runtime apply-config --pool hostpool-gpu-7 --set continuous_batch_window=32 --set prefetch_max_entries_per_session=50 --set kvcache_eviction_threshold=0.8
```

infra-bot: deploy started — job id: jb_2798123480. 2 nodes targeted for canary. Expected completion 90s.

Alex Park: adding a temporary routing policy to divert new sessions > 100k prompt length to fallback model rdx-medium-quant to avoid new large KV growth: ```
routing-rule add --match "prompt.length > 100000" --target rdx-medium-quant --priority 200
```

Devon Shah: good. also propose immediate manual termination of top offender session-93fa (if we confirm customer consent or emergency). any objections?

Laura Kim: we can evict that session from the cache only (no process kill) with: ```
redwoodctl runtime kvcache evict --session session-93fa --pool hostpool-gpu-7
``` Doing eviction first.

Mila Chen: eviction completed. memory dropped ~18% on hostpool-gpu-7 within 10s. seeing reduced paging. canary config finished on 2 nodes -> memory growth flattened.

Samira Patel: reached out to acme-marketing lead to explain emergency mitigation; they asked for timeline. I told them we'll follow up after stabilization and provide root cause.

Chris Ortega: traffic metrics post-hotpatch: 5m avg kvcache_used down from 92% -> 61% on canary nodes. per-token latency for /v1/chat/stream back to baseline. some requests still routed to old pool until rolling completes.

Devon Shah: plan: 1) complete rolling config to all hostpools in us-west-2 (ETA 10m). 2) run automated job to detect sessions that grow > 1.5x memory in 2m and throttle. 3) follow-up runbook addition for runaway-long-prompt detection.

Mila Chen: rolling completes at 2798123610. observed one regression when a new session kicked off with 200k prompt — routing rule worked and sent to rdx-medium-quant. no OOMs.

Laura Kim: opening a patch PR to make these settings defaults for hosted runtime and add feature flag to automatically cap prefetch for sessions over threshold. PR: https://github.com/redwood/re/runtime/pull/4182

Alex Park: root cause hypothesis: customers concatenating prior chat history into single prompt; continuous batching + prefix caching kept KV entries pinned because eviction policy favored recency not size. Combined with a scheduler regression that allowed oversized sessions through batching window.

Samira Patel: Customer impact assessment: ~2.1% of requests in us-west-2 experienced 5-10x latency for a 12-minute window. One enterprise customer saw ~140 errors in that window. No data corruption, just elevated latency/errors.

Chris Ortega: next actions for follow-up: - postmortem draft (Mila) - make runtime defaults safer (Laura) - add telemetry + alerts for session growth rate (Devon) - notify affected customers with timeline (Samira)

Mila Chen: handing off to Devon for overnight monitoring. I'll update the incident channel with postmortem skeleton. Devon, taking oncall in 30m.

Devon Shah: taking over. I'll keep watch for 2h and will escalate if memory climbs. slack escalation list updated.

infra-bot: hostpool rolling apply complete at 2798123698. No further OOMs observed.

Mila Chen: thanks team. quick notes appended to incident log; we'll follow up with a formal postmortem and the config PR review.

Devon Shah: added temporary Dashboard alert: "kvcache_session_growth_rate > 1.5x in 2m" -> pager to incidents. Also scheduled a canary test tomorrow that simulates concatenated long histories.

Samira Patel: support will send customer post-incident note by EOD.

Mila Chen: incident resolved -> severity downgraded. Closing pager thread at last_message_ts 2798123720. Remember to add runbook steps for: immediate session eviction, routing fallback, and default prefetch caps. :white_check_mark:
